rules.description: Agricultural cash wages count if employee receives at least $150 from one employer in the calendar year or employer expenditures for agricultural labor reach $2,500 in the year. The employer-wide alternative does not apply to the specified seasonal hand-harvest employee paid on a customary piece-rate basis, commuting daily from a permanent residence, who worked in agriculture less than 13 weeks in the preceding year. Remuneration paid in any medium other than cash, such as lodging, food, clothing or commodities, is excluded. Before August 7, 1995, SSA excluded noncash transfers from wages; from that date an economically cash-equivalent noncash transfer is tested as cash wages, based on actual transfer and dominion-and-control facts.

worked_examples.source_passage: Gavrielle operates a small family fruit farm. Gavrielle employs day laborers in the picking season to allow Gavrielle time to get the crops to market. Gavrielle doesn’t deduct the employees’ share of social security and Medicare taxes from their pay; instead, Gavrielle pays it on their behalf. When Gavrielle prepares the employees’ Forms W-2, Gavrielle adds each employee’s share of social security and Medicare taxes that Gavrielle paid to the employee’s wage income (box 1 of Form W-2), but doesn’t include it in box 3 (social security wages) or box 5 (Medicare wages and tips). For 2026, Gavrielle paid Dan $1,000 during the year. Gavrielle enters $1,076.50 in box 1 of Dan‘s Form W-2 ($1,000 wages plus $76.50 social security and Medicare taxes paid for Dan). Gavrielle enters $1,000.00 in boxes 3 and 5 of Dan’s Form W-2.

worked_examples.source_passage: A farm operator agrees to give an employee 30 head of cattle for services performed on the farm. The farm operator sells 100 head of cattle to a commodity purchaser. worked_examples.source_passage: A farm operator pays an employee $50 a month plus 10 head of cattle per month for services performed on the farm. The employee pays the farmer rent to maintain the cattle on the farm property in an area separate from the farm operator's livestock. The employee assumes the costs of feeding, maintaining, and transferring the cattle to the market for sale. The employee is paid directly by the commodity purchaser for the cattle. These facts indicate that the commodity payments are not wages because the employee exercises dominion and control over the cattle subsequent to receipt and bears the cost incident to ownership of the cattle.

cases.description: Pub. L. 95-216 section 351(d) applies the 1977 amendments "with respect to remuneration paid and services rendered after December 31, 1977". For pay on or after 1978-01-01 for nonbusiness work rendered before 1978 the clause has two readings, and CE1 states its choice (named_options, group section_351d_cash_test_date): the date paid decides, so such pay takes the $100 calendar-year test, threshold casual_cash_annual for the year paid, as threshold_id_by_case names, not this row's quarterly amount. 409(a)(6)(C) tests "cash remuneration paid by an employer in any calendar year". The other reading, that the amendments reach only pay both paid and for services rendered after 1977, keeps the $50 calendar-quarter test for this pay. The cited sources reach the pay under both tests: POMS RS 01901.520 C.1 imposes the $100 test "in any calendar year, subsequent to 1977", and C.2 keeps the $50 test for "nonbusiness work performed" from 1955 through 1977. nonprofit_1968_1977 gives the other reading's result for 409(p), which came from the same section 351. The case ranks below the farm, domestic, business and noncash cases, which the 1977 amendment did not change (review r6 M-6). Review r7 M-6 drops the earlier claim that election_work_1968 reads the same clause: it reads section 353(g), "remuneration paid after December 31, 1977".

cases.description: 411(c)'s closing sentence keeps 411(c)(4) in force, with no 1402(e) exemption, for "service performed by a member of a religious order who has taken a vow of poverty as a member of such order", so these duties are not self-employment. The 1967 amendments covered only "members of religious orders who have not taken a vow of poverty" (POMS NL 00711.065 1331). 410(a)(8)(A) lets an order's 3121(r) election make them covered employment, so religious_order_vow_of_poverty decides the service: the election, its retroactive quarters and members abroad. The case ranks first because that family decides a vowed member's service whatever this family's other facts are.

cases.description: POMS RS 01901.600 B.3.c: "Service performed by a duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed minister as a chaplain in the employ of the U.S., (including the Armed Services), wholly owned instrumentality of the U.S., the District of Columbia, a State or local governmental entity, a foreign government, or any of their political subdivisions, is not considered in the exercise of the ministry." A.3 says the same of service as a chaplain in the Armed Forces, a governmental entity or a government-owned and operated hospital. So no clergy case reaches it, whatever the minister's exemption: this family excludes nothing, and the government-service families decide the service (review r6 M-7). Ranked above every ministry case.

cases.description: Pub. L. 103-296 section 306 (the 26 U.S.C. 1402 notes): "Notwithstanding any other provision of law", an individual who performed 1402(c)(4) services "which are subject to tax under section 1401", where "such services were performed in Canada at a time when no agreement between the United States and Canada pursuant to section 233 of the Social Security Act ... was in effect" and the individual "was required to pay contributions on the earnings from such services under the social insurance system of Canada", may file a certificate "effective for taxable years ending after December 31, 1978, and before January 1, 1985". Paragraph (3) limits who may file; the exemption runs "with respect to services described in paragraphs (1) and (2)", which do not name contributions, and section 306(d) withholds credit only from "any income on which such tax would have been imposed but for such exemption". L. 103-296 section 306 (the 26 U.S.C. 1402 notes): "Notwithstanding any other provision of law", an individual who performed 1402(c)(4) services "which are subject to tax under section 1401", where "such services were performed in Canada at a time when no agreement between the United States and Canada pursuant to section 233 of the Social Security Act ... was in effect" and the individual "was required to pay contributions on the earnings from such services under the social insurance system of Canada", may file a certificate "effective for taxable years ending after December 31, 1978, and before January 1, 1985". Paragraph (3) limits who may file; the exemption runs "with respect to services described in paragraphs (1) and (2)", which do not name contributions, and section 306(d) withholds credit only from "any income on which such tax would have been imposed but for such exemption". So the certificate condition carries (3) as the person's eligibility, and the case reads this service's place and 1401 tax: the same minister's Canadian ministry on whose earnings no Canadian contributions were required is exempt too, while his ministry in the United States is not and reaches ministry_without_exemption_or_vow (review r7 M-1).

cases.description: Ranked first, where the agricultural deferral stood. The 409 notes and POMS date the end of agricultural treatment of farm domestic pay a year apart. On the notes' reading this row decides the pay: noncash pay is excluded, cash pay of $50 to $999 takes benefit_credit_transition_1994 (covered) and less fails the $1,000 test. On POMS's reading agricultural_service_1988 decides it: noncash pay is excluded, and cash pay is wages once the employer pays the employee $150 or more in the year or its expenditures for agricultural labor reach $2,500 (409(a)(7)(B)). The readings differ only for $50 to $149 from an employer spending less than $2,500 (covered, then excluded) and for less than $50 from one spending $2,500 or more (excluded, then covered), so the case reads those two cells (review r6 M-2; review r7 M-8(c): it had refused $150 to $999, which both readings cover).

citation.location: Social Security and Medicare Taxes; Not withholding the employee share; employer pays taxes on explicit 2026 $100 weekly cash pay example

worked_examples.source_passage: In 2026, you hire a household employee (who is an unrelated individual over age 18) to care for your child and agree to pay cash wages of $100 every Friday. You expect to pay your employee $3,000 or more for the year. You decide to pay your employee’s share of social security and Medicare taxes from your own funds. You pay your employee $100 every Friday without withholding any social security or Medicare taxes. For social security and Medicare tax purposes, your employee’s wages each payday are $100. For each wage payment, you will pay $15.30 when you pay the taxes. This is $7.65 ($6.20 for social security tax plus $1.45 for Medicare tax) to cover your employee’s share plus $7.65 ($6.20 for social security tax plus $1.45 for Medicare tax) for your share. For income tax purposes, your employee’s wages each payday are $107.65 ($100 + the $7.65 you will pay to cover your employee’s share of social security and Medicare taxes).

citation.location: Social Security and Medicare Taxes; withholding example, Mary Brown and Jane A. Oak

worked_examples.source_passage: On January 31, 2026, Mary Brown hired Jane A. Oak (who is an unrelated individual over age 18) to care for Mary’s child and agreed to pay cash wages of $70 every Friday. Jane worked for the remainder of the year (a total of 48 weeks). Jane didn’t give Mary a Form W-4 to request federal income tax withholding. The following is the information Mary will need to complete Schedule H (Form 1040), Form W-2, and Form W-3. Total cash wages paid to Jane $3,360.00 ($70 x 48 weeks) Jane’s share of: Social security tax $208.32 ($3,360 x 6.2% (0.062)) Medicare tax $48.72 ($3,360 x 1.45% (0.0145))

citations.authority: 26 C.F.R. 31.3121(b)(7)-2, April 1, 1998 edition, before T.D. 8794 (govinfo CFR XML, captured 2026-11-03)
citations.quote: Under section 3121(b)(7)(F), whether an employee is a member of a retirement system is determined on an entity-by-entity rather than a position-by-position basis. parameters.scope: Service as an election official or election worker (418(c)(8); 410(a)(7)(F)(iv)) in the employ of a State, a political subdivision or a wholly owned instrumentality (410(a)(7); 418(a)(1)). "State" here means one of the 50 States, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or the Virgin Islands. 410(h) makes the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam and American Samoa States for the subchapter; the family leaves the District of Columbia, Guam and American Samoa, whose service current 410(a)(7)(C)-(E) treat separately, to the open row state_local_territories_history_open. Grounds by case: the agreement cases (agreement_with_lower_threshold_member and agreement_with_statutory_threshold) take 418(b)(1), under which "State" for a section 418 agreement does not include the District of Columbia, Guam or American Samoa; agreement_with_lower_threshold_nonmember takes 418(b)(1) for the agreement and 410(a)(7)(F), which itself reaches "a State (other than the District of Columbia, Guam, or American Samoa)", for mandatory coverage; outside_agreement_nonmember applies 410(a)(7)(F), which itself reaches "a State (other than the District of Columbia, Guam, or American Samoa)"; outside_agreement_member applies the general 410(a)(7) exclusion, whose "State" is 410(h)'s, less the carve under 410(a)(7)(C)-(E) above. Other service falls to other families.

Membership goes entity by entity (26 C.F.R. 31.3121(b)(7)-2(c)(2)): a member of the county's qualified system through another county position is a member for the poll work too (Example 1), and a member only of another entity's system, the State's included, is not (Example 2).

citations.quote: An individual is employed full-time by a State and is a member of its retirement plan. The individual is also employed part-time by a city located in the State, but does not participate in the city's retirement plan. The services of the individual for the city are not excluded from employment under section 3121(b)(7), because the determination of whether services constitute employment for such purposes is made separately with respect to each political subdivision for which services are performed.

citations.authority: 26 C.F.R. 31.3121(b)(7)-2, April 1, 1998 edition, before T.D. 8794 (govinfo CFR XML, captured 2026-11-03)
citations.quote: Under section 3121(b)(7)(F), whether an employee is a member of a retirement system is determined on an entity-by-entity rather than a position-by-position basis. Thus, if an employee is a member of a retirement system with respect to service he or she performs in one position in the employ of a State, political subdivision or instrumentality thereof, the employee is generally treated as a member of a retirement system with respect to all service performed for the same State, political subdivision or instrumentality in any other positions. A State is a separate entity from its political subdivisions, and an instrumentality is a separate entity from the State or political subdivision by which it is owned for purposes of this rule.

parameters.scope: Service as an election official or election worker (418(c)(8); 410(a)(7)(F)(iv)) in the employ of a State, a political subdivision or a wholly owned instrumentality (410(a)(7); 418(a)(1)). "State" here means one of the 50 States, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or the Virgin Islands. 410(h) makes the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam and American Samoa States for the subchapter; the family leaves the District of Columbia, Guam and American Samoa, whose service current 410(a)(7)(C)-(E) treat separately, to the open row state_local_territories_history_open. Grounds by case: the agreement cases (agreement_with_lower_threshold_member and agreement_with_statutory_threshold) take 418(b)(1), under which "State" for a section 418 agreement does not include the District of Columbia, Guam or American Samoa; agreement_with_lower_threshold_nonmember takes 418(b)(1) for the agreement and 410(a)(7)(F), which itself reaches "a State (other than the District of Columbia, Guam, or American Samoa)", for mandatory coverage; outside_agreement_nonmember applies 410(a)(7)(F), which itself reaches "a State (other than the District of Columbia, Guam, or American Samoa)"; outside_agreement_member applies the general 410(a)(7) exclusion, whose "State" is 410(h)'s, less the carve under 410(a)(7)(C)-(E) above. Other service falls to other families.

residual_default.description: Federal service is covered when none of the stated statutory exclusion cases applies; apply the other families. This family does not read 410(a)'s base definition. Outside the United States, 410(a) makes service employment only (A)(ii) on or in connection with an American vessel or American aircraft under a contract of service entered into within the United States, or one during which the craft touches at a United States port, while the employee is employed on and in connection with it, "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either"; (B) "by a citizen or resident of the United States" (before 1984, "a citizen of the United States": Pub. L. 98-21 section 323(a)(2), for remuneration paid after 1983) as an employee (i) of an American employer or (ii) of a foreign affiliate of an American employer "during any period for which there is in effect an agreement, entered into pursuant to section 3121(l)" with respect to the affiliate (Pub. L. 98-21 section 321(b), for agreements entered into after April 20, 1983, wrote "American employer" for "a domestic corporation" and "affiliate" for "subsidiary"); or (C) "regardless of where or by whom performed", where an agreement under section 433 designates the service as employment or recognizes it as equivalent to employment (added by Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(a)(1), effective in taxable years beginning on or after April 20, 1983). No family in this registry reads these conditions, so neither this residual nor a covered case of this family reaches service abroad that none of them reaches: a noncitizen's before 1984, and a nonresident noncitizen's from 1984, that is not on or in connection with an American vessel or aircraft as (A)(ii) states and that no section 433 agreement designates (registry scope_gaps, review r6 M-5 and r7 H-2).

residual_default.description: Federal service is covered when no case matches; the cases apply in precedence order, first match wins. This family does not read 410(a)'s base definition. Outside the United States, 410(a) makes service employment only (A)(ii) on or in connection with an American vessel or American aircraft under a contract of service entered into within the United States, or one during which the craft touches at a United States port, while the employee is employed on and in connection with it, "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either"; (B) "by a citizen or resident of the United States" (before 1984, "a citizen of the United States": Pub. L. 98-21 section 323(a)(2), for remuneration paid after 1983) as an employee (i) of an American employer or (ii) of a foreign affiliate of an American employer "during any period for which there is in effect an agreement, entered into pursuant to section 3121(l)" with respect to the affiliate (Pub. L. 98-21 section 321(b), for agreements entered into after April 20, 1983, wrote "American employer" for "a domestic corporation" and "affiliate" for "subsidiary"); or (C) "regardless of where or by whom performed", where an agreement under section 433 designates the service as employment or recognizes it as equivalent to employment (added by Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(a)(1), effective in taxable years beginning on or after April 20, 1983). No family in this registry reads these conditions, so neither this residual nor a covered case of this family reaches service abroad that none of them reaches: a noncitizen's before 1984, and a nonresident noncitizen's from 1984, that is not on or in connection with an American vessel or aircraft as (A)(ii) states and that no section 433 agreement designates (registry scope_gaps, review r6 M-5 and r7 H-2).

parameters.scope: 410(a)(5) and (a)(6) reach only service "in the employ of the United States or any instrumentality of the United States", so every case this row decides by an exclusion, or leaves open, names that level; a State, local, District of Columbia, tribal, foreign or private employer's worker reaches the residual, and the other families decide the service. first_hired_after_1983 names the level too, so a non-Federal new hire reaches the residual. The Army Corps student aide and the reemployed annuitant open cases rest on POMS RS 01901.340, which addresses Federal employment.
parameters.section_2601d3_delay: Section 2601(d)(3) delays 410(a)(5)(G) coverage to the first month after the 30-day period of 2601(d)(1), which ends 30 days after July 18, 1984, or of 2601(d)(2), which reaches an individual "not in the employ of the United States or an instrumentality thereof" on July 18, 1984 and ends 30 days after the individual first returns to legislative-branch service after that date, a return that must fall within 365 days after the individual "was last in the employ of the United States". The (d)(1) delay ends before 1987; a (d)(2) delay has no outer date. Cases legislative_lump_sum_after_1983 and legislative_ceased_coverage_after_1983 carry the clause, as the 1984-1986 row's do. Whether the delay also holds back the Pub. L. 100-647 section 8015(c) after-official rule in the delay months is open (case after_official_during_2601d3_delay).

residual_default.description: Federal service is covered when no case matches; the cases apply in precedence order, first match wins. This family does not read 410(a)'s base definition. Outside the United States, 410(a) makes service employment only (A)(ii) on or in connection with an American vessel or American aircraft under a contract of service entered into within the United States, or one during which the craft touches at a United States port, while the employee is employed on and in connection with it, "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either"; (B) "by a citizen or resident of the United States" (before 1984, "a citizen of the United States": Pub. L. 98-21 section 323(a)(2), for remuneration paid after 1983) as an employee (i) of an American employer or (ii) of a foreign affiliate of an American employer "during any period for which there is in effect an agreement, entered into pursuant to section 3121(l)" with respect to the affiliate (Pub. L. 98-21 section 321(b), for agreements entered into after April 20, 1983, wrote "American employer" for "a domestic corporation" and "affiliate" for "subsidiary"); or (C) "regardless of where or by whom performed", where an agreement under section 433 designates the service as employment or recognizes it as equivalent to employment (added by Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(a)(1), effective in taxable years beginning on or after April 20, 1983). No family in this registry reads these conditions, so neither this residual nor a covered case of this family reaches service abroad that none of them reaches: a noncitizen's before 1984, and a nonresident noncitizen's from 1984, that is not on or in connection with an American vessel or aircraft as (A)(ii) states and that no section 433 agreement designates (registry scope_gaps, review r6 M-5 and r7 H-2).

parameters.effective_basis_description: Pub. L. 104-188 section 1116(a)(3)(A): "The amendments made by this subsection shall apply to remuneration paid-- (i) after December 31, 1994, and (ii) after December 31, 1984, and before January 1, 1995, unless the payor treated such remuneration (when paid) as being subject to tax under chapter 21 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986." parameters.historical_default_cash_rule: No cash remuneration apart from the catch share or sale-proceeds share when the payor treated remuneration as FICA-taxable; otherwise the expressly conditional 1996 clarification applies.

source_disagreement_resolution.basis: Public Law 104-188 section 1116(a)(3)(A) applies the 1996 amendments to remuneration paid after December 31, 1984, and before January 1, 1995, unless the payor treated it (when paid) as subject to FICA tax. Where they apply, their terms are current_statute_crew_test: fewer than 10 crew averaged over the preceding 4 calendar quarters, and cash of at most $100 per trip that is contingent on a minimum catch and paid for traditional additional duties. Where the payor treated the pay as FICA-taxed, the earlier tests in conditional_1996_clarification.if_does_not_apply govern, as in unamended_cfr_cash_prohibition. POMS RS 01901.280 A.2 (no more than 10 crew over the previous calendar quarter, no minimum-catch condition; "effective with remuneration paid after 1994", and by its NOTE also for 1985 through 1994 "unless the remuneration was treated by the payor as wages when paid") is recorded as poms_crew_test and is not operative. For pay the 1996 amendments reach, 26 U.S.C. 3121(b)(20)(A) bars only "any cash remuneration" beyond what it allows, and 20 CFR 404.1031(a)(1) only "any cash pay", where 410(a)(20)(A) bars "any additional compensation"; that reading is recorded as irc_and_cfr_cash_only_bar (the Code's crew and cash terms; the CFR's other, unamended terms stay in unamended_cfr_cash_prohibition) and is not operative, because a crew member whose only extra pay is non-cash is covered on either reading: in employment under 410(a), or in self-employment under 20 CFR 404.1031(b).

parameters.clause_a_employment_test: 410(a)(4)(A) is met when the individual is employed on and in connection with the craft while it is outside the United States; it then reaches that employment's service in the United States too.
parameters.clause_a_gloss_basis: The in-port reading ("including service done within the U.S. if some part of the employee's service is done outside the U.S.") comes from POMS RS 01901.170 B, headed "1951 THROUGH 1954"; section A (1955 and later) states the same employment test, "employed on or in connection with such vessel or aircraft when outside the United States", without the gloss. IRS Publication 15 (2026) restates the reading for resident aliens in 2026: "Exempt if any part of service as crew member of foreign vessel or aircraft is performed outside the United States." The row applies it to every year from 1968 under clause (A)'s words, "is employed on and in connection with such vessel or aircraft when outside the United States", as the captured code prints them; the LII amendment notes list one entry for subsection (a)(4), the 1954 act's, and describe only the clause (B) conditions it added.

cases.description: Under an actual certificate in effect for the service, these employees are covered: those who signed the List of Concurring Employees (Form SS-15a) filed with the certificate, and those hired afterwards (NPO503, "the employees who signed the SS-15a, as well as those hired afterwards, were covered"; NPO505; RS 01901.540 C.1, C.4). An employee added by a supplemental list, which counts only if filed "prior to the expiration of the twenty-fourth month following the calendar quarter in which the certificate is filed" (1958 (k)(1) note; C.6 NOTE), is covered only for service from the first day of the calendar quarter in which that list was filed (1958 (k)(1) note). An employee who, after the quarter in which the certificate was filed for a 3121(k)(1)(E) group, became a member of that group is covered too: the 1958 (a)(8)(B) note makes the exclusion inapplicable to her service during the certificate's period. A worker hired between the filing and the effective date is covered from the effective date. Former 410(a)(10)(A)'s $50 quarterly remuneration test applies (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_quarter).

L. 95-216 section 312(c) note: where service for an organization deemed under 3121(k)(4) to have filed a certificate, performed before July 1, 1977, is not employment because 3121(k)(4)(C) makes the deemed certificate inapplicable to it, the remuneration "shall, upon the request of such individual (filed on or before April 15, 1980", with the taxes, be deemed remuneration for employment; POMS RS 01901.540 D.8 says the same. On either reading of the open case below the service is then covered, subject to former 410(a)(10)(A)'s $50 quarterly test (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_quarter), which the note's "would constitute employment ... in the absence of such section 3121(k)(4)(C)" keeps.

L. 95-216 section 312(c) note treats service for an organization deemed under 3121(k)(4) to have filed a certificate, performed "on or after the first day of the applicable period described in subparagraph (A)(ii) of such section 3121(k)(4) and before July 1, 1977", as service that "does not constitute employment ... because the waiver certificate which the organization is deemed to have filed is made inapplicable to such service by section 3121(k)(4)(C)", and POMS RS 01901.540 D.8 describes the 1977 Amendments as "forgiving the tax liability of organizations through 6/30/77 when the employer stopped paying taxes before 10/19/76 because no waiver certificates were filed". The case's condition is that service, so former 410(a)(8)(B) excludes it unless the employee made a timely 312(c) request (deemed_waiver_section_312c_request, ranked above). Ranked above deemed_waiver_all_employees, whose condition this worker also meets: 3121(k)(4)(C) took this service back out of the deemed certificate's period (review r6 M-2 settles the round-5 open case on these two captures). Review r7 M-9: the window is each quarter, after the organization stopped paying, for which it paid no taxes, since D.8 forgives "the tax liability" through 6/30/77 and a quarter whose taxes were paid leaves none; it had read "after the last calendar quarter for which the organization paid the taxes", which missed an organization that resumed paying, whose unpaid quarters then took deemed_waiver_all_employees.

Pub. L. 98-21 section 102(c) keeps "the provisions of sections 2 and 3 of Public Law 94–563" in effect. The note's "would constitute employment" keeps former 410(a)(10)(A)'s $50 quarterly test (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_quarter). Ranked above no_effective_waiver, which this service also meets (it falls before the certificate's period); the note lifts it.

cases.description: The Pub. L. 86-778 section 105(b) note (as amended by Pub. L. 89-97 section 316(c)): where "an individual performed service in the employ of an organization with respect to which remuneration was paid before the first day of the calendar quarter in which the organization filed a waiver certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1)", the service is excepted by former 410(a)(8)(B), and "such organization paid, on or before the due date of the tax return for the calendar quarter before the calendar quarter in which the organization filed a certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code, any amount, as taxes imposed by sections 3101 and 3111" on it, then on the individual's request "the remuneration with respect to which the amount has been paid as taxes shall be deemed to constitute remuneration for employment for purposes of title II of such Act" (paragraph (1)). Paragraph (2) applies it only where the organization, "on or before the date on which the request described in paragraph (1) is made, has filed a certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code"; paragraph (3): "Paragraph (1) shall not apply with respect to an individual who is employed by the organization referred to in paragraph (2) on the date the certificate is filed."; paragraph (4) bars it after a credit or refund of the taxes unless the amount "is repaid before January 1, 1968, or, if later, the first day of the third year after the year in which the organization filed a certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code"; paragraph (5): "Paragraph (1) shall not apply to any service performed for the organization in a period for which a certificate filed pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code is not in effect." So the case keeps the actual-certificate text. Paragraph (1)(B)'s "such service would have constituted employment as defined in section 210 of such Act" keeps former 410(a)(10)(A)'s $50 quarterly remuneration test (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_quarter). Ranked above waiver_retroactive_period_hire_unlisted and waiver_nonconcurring_existing_employee, which such an employee can also meet; the note lifts both.

cases.open_reason: NONPROFIT_RETROACTIVE_HIRE_UNSETTLED: a certificate filed after 1965 may take effect up to 20 quarters before its filing (RS 01901.540 C.3.b). For an employee hired after that effective date and still employed, or already gone, when it was filed, who never signed the Form SS-15a, RS 01901.540 C.4 covers "all employees hired after the effective date of the certificate", while NL 00902.500 NPO505 covers only those who signed among "persons employed at the time of the request" and NPO506 tells an unsigned employee "Since you were employed by the organization when Social Security coverage was requested, your service is not counted". No capture holds the text of former 410(a)(8)(B)'s clause (ii): the 1976 amendment note shows only that its clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) each used the word "filed", and the 1958 amendment note paraphrases only its 3121(k)(1)(E) group provisions. So the statute's own words on which unsigned employees hired before the filing a certificate reached are not captured, and the case refuses.

A supplemental list counts only if filed "prior to the expiration of the twenty-fourth month following the calendar quarter in which the certificate is filed" (1958 (k)(1) note). cases.description: The 1977 amendment note to 3121(b)(10) says Pub. L. 95-216 section 356(c) "struck out subpar. (A) which related to service performed in any calendar quarter in the employ of any organization exempt from income tax under section 501(a) (other than an organization described in section 401(a) or under section 521, if the remuneration for such service was less than $50", and the 42 U.S.C. 410 note on subsec. (a)(10) says Pub. L. 95-216 "struck out subpar. (A) which related to service performed in the employ of any exempt organization under section 101 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1939". Neither limits the test to 501(c)(3) organizations, so the row applies it to service for another 501(a) organization, which former 410(a)(8)(B) does not exclude (see the residual): covered above former 410(a)(10)(A)'s $50 quarterly test (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_quarter). The 3121 note's parenthesis never closes, so its words do not settle whether "or under section 521" put 521 cooperatives inside the test, as 3121(a)(16) does from 1978, or inside the 401(a) exception. The text leaves 521 out; a 521 cooperative's employee takes the residual.

cases.description: Under an actual certificate in effect for the service, these employees are covered: those who signed the List of Concurring Employees (Form SS-15a) filed with the certificate, and those hired afterwards (NPO503, "the employees who signed the SS-15a, as well as those hired afterwards, were covered"; NPO505; RS 01901.540 C.1, C.4). An employee added by a supplemental list, which counts only if filed "prior to the expiration of the twenty-fourth month following the calendar quarter in which the certificate is filed" (1958 (k)(1) note; C.6 NOTE), is covered only for service from the first day of the calendar quarter in which that list was filed (1958 (k)(1) note). An employee who, after the quarter in which the certificate was filed for a 3121(k)(1)(E) group, became a member of that group is covered too: the 1958 (a)(8)(B) note makes the exclusion inapplicable to her service during the certificate's period. A worker hired between the filing and the effective date is covered from the effective date. From 1978, 409(a)(14)'s $100 annual remuneration test applies (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_year).

cases.description: The Pub. L. 86-778 section 105(b) note (as amended by Pub. L. 89-97 section 316(c)): where "an individual performed service in the employ of an organization with respect to which remuneration was paid before the first day of the calendar quarter in which the organization filed a waiver certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1)", the service is excepted by former 410(a)(8)(B), and "such organization paid, on or before the due date of the tax return for the calendar quarter before the calendar quarter in which the organization filed a certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code, any amount, as taxes imposed by sections 3101 and 3111" on it, then on the individual's request "the remuneration with respect to which the amount has been paid as taxes shall be deemed to constitute remuneration for employment for purposes of title II of such Act" (paragraph (1)). Paragraph (2) applies it only where the organization, "on or before the date on which the request described in paragraph (1) is made, has filed a certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code"; paragraph (3): "Paragraph (1) shall not apply with respect to an individual who is employed by the organization referred to in paragraph (2) on the date the certificate is filed."; paragraph (4) bars it after a credit or refund of the taxes unless the amount "is repaid before January 1, 1968, or, if later, the first day of the third year after the year in which the organization filed a certificate pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code"; paragraph (5): "Paragraph (1) shall not apply to any service performed for the organization in a period for which a certificate filed pursuant to section 3121(k)(1) of such Code is not in effect." So the case keeps the actual-certificate text. Paragraph (1)(B)'s "such service would have constituted employment as defined in section 210 of such Act" keeps the $100 annual remuneration test (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_year). Ranked above waiver_retroactive_period_hire_unlisted and waiver_nonconcurring_existing_employee, which such an employee can also meet; the note lifts both.

cases.open_reason: NONPROFIT_RETROACTIVE_HIRE_UNSETTLED: a certificate filed after 1965 may take effect up to 20 quarters before its filing (RS 01901.540 C.3.b). For an employee hired after that effective date and still employed, or already gone, when it was filed, who never signed the Form SS-15a, RS 01901.540 C.4 covers "all employees hired after the effective date of the certificate", while NL 00902.500 NPO505 covers only those who signed among "persons employed at the time of the request" and NPO506 tells an unsigned employee "Since you were employed by the organization when Social Security coverage was requested, your service is not counted". No capture holds the text of former 410(a)(8)(B)'s clause (ii): the 1976 amendment note shows only that its clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) each used the word "filed", and the 1958 amendment note paraphrases only its 3121(k)(1)(E) group provisions. So the statute's own words on which unsigned employees hired before the filing a certificate reached are not captured, and the case refuses.

C.4 reaches only hires after the effective date, and the 1958 (a)(8)(B) note only employees who joined the certificate's 3121(k)(1)(E) group after its filing quarter. A supplemental list counts only if filed "prior to the expiration of the twenty-fourth month following the calendar quarter in which the certificate is filed" (1958 (k)(1) note). So these sources leave this employee's service excluded by former 410(a)(8)(B), except where section_105b_departed_employee_request, ranked above, applies: Pub. L. 86-778 section 105(b) deems the remuneration wages on the request of an employee no longer employed when the certificate was filed.

The 401(a) half of the same disagreement is the open case section_401a_trust_small_remuneration; review r7 M-8(e) opens this half, which the row had closed by following 3121(a)(16). cases.description: From 1978, 3121(a)(16) excludes "remuneration paid by an organization exempt from income tax under section 501(a) (other than an organization described in section 401(a)) or under section 521 in any calendar year to an employee for service rendered in the employ of such organization, if the remuneration paid in such year by the organization to the employee for such service is less than $100". It reaches exempt organizations beyond 501(c)(3), whose service former 410(a)(8)(B) does not exclude, so that service is covered above the $100 annual test (threshold nonprofit_remuneration_year), as the row's threshold concept states. The title II text, 409(a)(14) (409(p) as Pub. L. 95-216 added it), reads "Remuneration paid by an organization exempt from income tax under section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986" and names neither the 401(a) exception nor 521. The case follows 3121(a)(16) for the other organizations; a 401(a) trust and a 521 cooperative paying less than $100 in the year reach the open cases section_401a_trust_small_remuneration and cooperative_521_small_remuneration (review r7 M-8(e)).

cases.description: The Social Security Act's 409 and the Code's 3121(a)(16) state the $100 rule for exempt organizations differently: 3121(a)(16) carves out "an organization described in section 401(a)", while the 409 text the 1984 row quotes names any "organization exempt from income tax under section 501". Neither text changes at 1984, so both rows open the question instead of choosing (review r6 M-8). The case reads the $100 amount both texts share: at $100 or more in the year both readings cover the pay, so the case does not reach it (review r7 M-8(b)).

cases.description: 410(a)(8)(A) excludes order duties by "a member of a religious order" unless an order election is in effect, and 411(c)'s closing sentence keeps 411(c)(4)'s exclusion from self-employment for every member "who has taken a vow of poverty as a member of such order". Neither limits the exclusion to an active member, so a vowed member retired for old age or total disability is excluded too. 410(a)(8)(A) lifts the exclusion only "if an election of coverage under section 3121(r) ... is in effect with respect to such order, or with respect to the autonomous subdivision thereof to which such member belongs", so another subdivision's election leaves it in place (3121(r)(1)(B)).

when.religious_order_service: member of a religious order who has taken a vow of poverty as a member of such order, performing duties required by such order

cases.description: POMS RS 01901.620 B.4: a member's services outside the United States are covered under the election only if the member is a United States citizen; otherwise the vow-of-poverty exclusion still applies. 410(a)(C), effective in taxable years beginning on or after April 20, 1983, makes service employment "regardless of where or by whom performed" where an agreement under section 433 designates it as employment or recognizes it as equivalent, so the case reads only service no such agreement designates (review r7 low 9).Noncovered whether or not an election is in effect: with no election 410(a)(8)(A) excludes the duties (vow_duties_without_election), and with one this member is outside what 3121(r) makes employment, so the case reads no election and ranks above election_status_not_established (review r6 M-2).

cases.description: 26 U.S.C. 3121(r)(3)(A): where the order designates a date before the quarter of filing, "the election shall apply to services performed before the quarter in which the certificate is filed only if the member performing such services was a member at the time such services were performed and is living on the first day of the quarter in which such certificate is filed". For this member's pre-filing service no election applies, so the vow-of-poverty exclusion stands.

cases.description: 3121(r)(2) defines a member "For purposes of this subsection" as one who performs tasks usually required "(and to the extent usually required)" of an active member and is not retired for old age or total disability, and 3121(r)(1)(C) deems only such a member's duties to be employment. A vowed member outside that definition gets no deemed wages under the election, and 411(c)'s closing sentence keeps the vow-of-poverty exclusion from self-employment, so the order election does not cover her duties.Noncovered whether or not an election is in effect: with no election 410(a)(8)(A) excludes the duties (vow_duties_without_election), and with one this member is outside what 3121(r) makes employment, so the case reads no election and ranks above election_status_not_established (review r6 M-2).

when.religious_order_service: member of a religious order who has taken a vow of poverty as a member of such order but does not perform the tasks usually required of an active member of such order to the extent usually required, or is considered retired because of old age or total disability (outside 3121(r)(2)), performing duties required by such order

cases.description: 3121(r)(1)(C) deems the order duties of a member, as 3121(r)(2) defines one (active, and not retired for old age or total disability), to be performed as an employee of the order; use the value of perquisites subject to the statutory floor. A subdivision's election applies only "to all current and future members of such order who belong to such subdivision" (3121(r)(1)(B)).POMS RS 01901.620 B.4 conditions a member's service abroad on the election, citizenship (from 1984, citizenship or residence) and membership: "Services performed by members of religious orders working outside the U.S. are covered if: • the order has elected coverage, • the member is a U.S. citizen, or effective January 1, 1984, a resident alien, and • the individual remains a member of the order even though their services may be directed by a third party outside the U.S., the right to direct and control remains with the member's order within the U.S." Its third bullet makes remaining a member the condition: direction by a third party abroad leaves the right to direct and control with the order, so no case excludes a member abroad on control alone (review r6 M-4; POMS NL 00711.065 1331.3 B lists the same three conditions).

worked_examples.source_passage: Pat Brown and Chris Green are members of a religious order and have taken vows of poverty. They renounce all claims to their earnings. The earnings belong to the order. Pat is a licensed attorney. The superiors of the order instructed Pat to get a job with a law firm. Pat joined a law firm as an employee and, as requested, the firm made the salary payments directly to the order. Chris is a secretary. The superiors of the order instructed Chris to accept a job with the business office of the church that supervises the order. Chris took the job and gave all earnings to the order. Chris' services are duties required by the order. Chris is acting as an agent of the order and not as an employee of a third party. Chris doesn't include the earnings in gross income, and they aren't subject to income tax withholding or to social security and Medicare tax under FICA or SECA.

cases.description: Mandatory coverage, including optionals and ineligibles, unless a statutory exclusion applies. Membership only in a system that fails the IRS qualified-system standards (POMS SL 50001.501 B) does not defeat it (410(a)(7)(F)). 410(a)(7)(F) asks whether the individual is "a member of a retirement system of such State, political subdivision, or instrumentality", and 26 C.F.R. 31.3121(b)(7)-2(c)(2) answers it "on an entity-by-entity rather than a position-by-position basis": a member through one position "is generally treated as a member of a retirement system with respect to all service performed for the same State, political subdivision or instrumentality in any other positions" (Example 1: a county plan member's part-time county service in a position the plan excludes stays excluded), while "A State is a separate entity from its political subdivisions" (Example 2: a State plan member's part-time service for a city whose plan she is not in is not excluded). A statewide system counts when the employing entity takes part in it: (e)(2)(v) speaks of "a retirement system maintained by multiple States, political subdivisions or instrumentalities thereof (including the current employer)", (d)(4)(ii) of "a school district that participates in a state-wide teachers' retirement system", 418(d)(6)(A) contemplates a system that "covers positions of employees of the State and positions of employees of one or more political subdivisions of the State", and POMS SL 30001.334 F.1 describes MERS as "a statewide system covering all municipal employees". Benefits from service for another entity count only as (d)(4)(ii) (a re-hired annuitant of the same system) and (e)(2)(v) allow. The April 1, 1998 edition, before either later amendment, states (c)(2) and its examples in the same words.

A State is a separate entity from its political subdivisions, and an instrumentality is a separate entity from the State or political subdivision by which it is owned for purposes of this rule.

citations.quote: Under section 3121(b)(7)(F), whether an employee is a member of a retirement system is determined on an entity-by-entity rather than a position-by-position basis. Thus, if an employee is a member of a retirement system with respect to service he or she performs in one position in the employ of a State, political subdivision or instrumentality thereof, the employee is generally treated as a member of a retirement system with respect to all service performed for the same State, political subdivision or instrumentality in any other positions. A State is a separate entity from its political subdivisions, and an instrumentality is a separate entity from the State or political subdivision by which it is owned for purposes of this rule.

worked_examples.source_passage: A referendum was held among all the eligible members of the Municipal Employees Retirement System (MERS), a statewide system covering all municipal employees. A was an employee of City X and voted against Social Security coverage. After the coverage was extended to the retirement system coverage group, A terminated his employment with City X and entered private employment. Under the rules of MERS, A retained his membership in MERS. Two years later, City X reemployed A. The State holds that he is not a new member of MERS. A is not a new member for purposes of coverage. He retains his initial choice of "No" coverage.

citation.authority: SSA State and Local Coverage Handbook, POMS SL 30001.334, revision January 29, 2020

worked_examples.source_passage: A referendum was held among all the eligible members of MERS, a statewide system covering all municipal employees. A was an employee of City X and voted against coverage. After coverage was extended to the retirement system coverage group, A terminated his employment with City X and entered private employment. A withdrew his contributions from the retirement system. Two years later, City X reemployed A. The State holds that he is a new member of MERS. A is a new member for purposes of coverage and is covered compulsorily.

A City’s Section 218 Agreement excludes part-time positions that require less than 20 hours of work per week. The City’s cafeteria has part-time employees who work part-time 15 hours per week. The City’s retirement system membership is only for employees who work in full-time positions. Therefore, part-time employees of the cafeteria are subject to mandatory Social Security and Medicare.

cases.description: 411(a): net earnings from self-employment are the gross income "derived by an individual from any trade or business carried on by such individual", less attributable deductions, "plus his distributive share ... from any trade or business carried on by a partnership of which he is a member". An amount that is neither is not this person's net earnings. 411(c) gives "trade or business" its section 162 meaning less the services it lists (public office, employee service other than (c)(2)(A)-(G), railroad service, exempt ministry and Christian Science practice, and service during a 1402(g) exemption); the families for those services apply those limits and their exceptions. A partner's guaranteed payment under section 707(c) is not her distributive share, but it is her net earnings: 411(a)(12) excludes a limited partner's share "other than guaranteed payments described in section 707(c)", and the 1985 Form 1040 instructions say to "include your entire share of earnings from a partnership, including any guaranteed payments". And 411(a)(5) assigns community income to one spouse: before taxable years including October 1980, former 411(a)(5)(A) treated a community business's gross income and deductions as the husband's unless the wife exercised substantially all of the management and control, whether or not he carried it on. Neither amount is excluded here; self_employment_limited_partner and self_employment_community_income decide them.

cases.description: The condition reaches only contributions "not included in the minister's gross income". 411(a) starts from "the gross income, as computed under subtitle A" of the Code; before July 18, 1984 the clause read "chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1939", and Pub. L. 98-369 section 2663(a)(8)(A) substituted "subtitle A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954", an amendment "not to be construed as changing or affecting any right, liability, status, or interpretation which existed". From taxable years beginning after 1972 411(a)(7) has a minister compute net earnings without sections 107 and 119 (Pub. L. 85-239) and 911 and 931 (Pub. L. 92-603), and no other exclusion, so an amount subtitle A leaves out of gross income stays out of net earnings, as in the 1987 row's case of the same text. Review r7 M-4 closes the case on these captures: its second reading ("No captured rule excludes the amount") named no source, and the exclusion needs none beyond 411(a)'s start. Each year's subtitle A limits decide which contributions the condition reaches; a contribution included in gross income misses it and the covered residual counts it.

worked_examples.source_passage: Pastor Leslie Adams receives an annual salary of $39,000 as a full-time minister. The $39,000 includes $5,000 that is designated as a rental allowance to pay utilities. His church owns a parsonage that has a fair rental value of $12,000 per year. The church gives Pastor Adams the use of the parsonage. Pastor Adams isn’t exempt from SE tax and must include $51,000 ($39,000 plus $12,000) when figuring his net earnings for SE tax purposes.

worked_examples.source_passage: Example 5. J owned a farm several miles from the town in which he lived. He rented the farm to K under an ar­ rangement which contemplated J’s mate­ rial participation in the management of production of wheat. J furnished one- half the seed and fertilizer and all the farm equipment and livestock. He em­ ployed H to perform all the services in advising, consulting, and inspecting which were contemplated by the arrange­ ment, effective with taxable years begin­ ning after December 31, 1973. J is not materially participating in the manage­ ment of production of wheat by K. The work done by J’s employee, H, is not attributable to J in determining the ex­ tent of J’s participation. J’s rental in­ come from the arrangement is not to be included in computing his net earn­ ings from self-employment.

worked_examples.source_passage: Example 6. J is not materially participating in the management of pro­ duction of wheat by K because the work done by X Bank is not attributable to J in determining the extent of J’s par­ ticipation. J’s rental income from the arrangement would not be included in computing his net earnings from self- employment.

cases.description: 26 U.S.C. 1401(c): "During any period in which there is in effect an agreement entered into pursuant to section 233 of the Social Security Act with any foreign country, the self-employment income of an individual shall be exempt" (an individual, not a minister alone) to the extent the agreement subjects it "exclusively to the laws applicable to the social security system of such foreign country". Pub. L. 95-216 section 317(b)(1) added the subsection ("Subsec. (c). Pub. L. 95–216, § 317(b)(1) , added subsec. (c)."), and section 317(a) added section 233 itself (42 U.S.C. 433, "as added Pub. L. 95–216, title III, § 317(a) , Dec. 20, 1977"), whose (c)(1)(B)(i) has every agreement place self-employment in one system "but not under both". Neither captured page gives section 317 another date (the 1401 page's Effective Date of 1977 Amendment note, section 104, covers title I only), so the condition carries the limit the subsection states, an agreement under section 233 in effect for the period, and no worker meets it before December 20, 1977. Pub. L. 98-21 section 124(b) redesignated the subsection (d) and Pub. L. 101-508 made it (c) again; Pub. L. 108-203 section 415 replaced "to taxes or contributions for similar purposes under" with "exclusively to the laws applicable to", and a person subject only to the partner country's laws meets both wordings. Review r7 M-2 dates the exemption on these captures; the pre-1983 open cases it closes rested on Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(c), the date of 411(b)'s section 433 exception, not of 1401(c). Publication 517 (2025) states the exception for ministers and points to Pub. 54's "Bilateral Social Security (Totalization) Agreements", the guide for citizens and resident aliens abroad. It overrides territorial_resident and cnmi_noncitizen_resident: on either CNMI reading the agreement leaves the person subject only to the foreign country's laws.

cases.description: Pub. L. 90-248 section 122(c)(2): "any individual who in 1968 is in a position to which the amendments made by such subsections apply may make an irrevocable election not to have such amendments apply to the fees he receives in 1968 and every year thereafter". Those amendments reach only a position of a State or a political subdivision "compensated solely on a fee basis": 411(c)(1)'s public-office exception and 411(c)(2)(E)'s employee rule. So the election displaces nothing for fees received outside such a position (as a contractor, say); they take the other cases or the residual.

cases.description: Former 411(a)(13)(C), which the 1986 amendment note quotes: "if the amount of such remuneration from an employer for the taxable year is less than $100, such remuneration from that employer shall not be included in self-employment income". So pay from an employer below the gate is out of self-employment income whatever the person's other earnings, and the combined floors of the other cases never reach it; electing_church_1984_1985's threshold ($100 from one employer) excludes it the same way. Review r7 M-5: round 6's low 3 sent such pay to the residual's $400 floor, which counted it toward $400. The case ranks first; one employer's pay meets either this text or the other cases' "at least $100" text, not both. For a fiscal year that began in 1983, this applies to remuneration for electing-church service performed on or after 1984-01-01 (Pub. L. 98-369 section 2603(e)). For 1984-1985 the ministry carve-out rests on those notes alone: 411(i)(4)'s "(and are not described in section 410(a)(8)(A) of this title)" came with Pub. L. 99-514 section 1882(b)(2)(A) in 1986 (review r7 low 7).

cases.open_reason: STUDENT_NURSE_SERVICE_BEYOND_TRAINING_UNSETTLED: 42 U.S.C. 410(a)(13) excludes "Service performed as a student nurse in the employ of a hospital or a nurses’ training school by an individual who is enrolled and is regularly attending classes in a nurses’ training school chartered or approved pursuant to State law", and POMS RS 01901.760 lists only those conditions ("Beginning 1/1/40, service performed as a student nurse in the employ of a hospital or nurses' training school is not covered if:"). POMS RS 01901.760 also says "The intent of Congress is to exclude student nurse employment: • that is part-time; • when the only service performed is incidental to the student's training; and • when the remuneration for services is nominal.", and IRS Publication 15 (2026) lists the exemption as "3. Student nurse performing part-time services for nominal earnings at hospital as incidental part of training." No capture settles whether the exclusion reaches a student nurse's service that is not part-time, not incidental to training or not for nominal pay, so such service refuses.

citations.quote: NOTE: Postdoctoral students, postdoctoral fellows, medical residents, and medical interns, are not considered students because the services they perform are not incidental to, and for the purpose of, participating in a course of study.

If the student's main purpose is pursuing a course of study rather than earning a livelihood, SSA considers this person to be a student and their work is not considered employment. Also, the student must carry at least a half-time academic workload.

A worker is not considered a student if the individual is: • eligible to participate in a retirement plan or annuity established or maintained by the institution, or would be eligible to participate if age and service requirements are met, or; • eligible for reduced tuition, or; • classified by the institution as a career employee.

The exclusion applies only during periods of regular school attendance, including the regular academic year and summer session. The exclusion does not apply to work done during school breaks of more than five weeks if the student is not attending school.
Services performed on holidays, weekends, and between semesters falling within the academic year when classes are not scheduled are excluded.
This is true even though the student was enrolled and regularly attending classes in the school during the previous year and expects to return to school the following year.
Effective Dates: 08/15/2024 - Present

scope_gaps.gap: No family in this registry reads 410(a)'s base definition of employment. Within the United States, service is employment "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either" (clause (A)(i)). Outside the United States, 410(a) makes service employment only (A)(ii) on or in connection with an American vessel or American aircraft under a contract of service entered into within the United States, or one during which the craft touches at a United States port, while the employee is employed on and in connection with it, "irrespective of the citizenship or residence of either"; (B) "by a citizen or resident of the United States" (before 1984, "a citizen of the United States": Pub. L. 98-21 section 323(a)(2), for remuneration paid after 1983) as an employee (i) of an American employer or (ii) of a foreign affiliate of an American employer "during any period for which there is in effect an agreement, entered into pursuant to section 3121(l)" with respect to the affiliate (Pub. L. 98-21 section 321(b), for agreements entered into after April 20, 1983, wrote "American employer" for "a domestic corporation" and "affiliate" for "subsidiary"); or (C) "regardless of where or by whom performed", where an agreement under section 433 designates the service as employment or recognizes it as equivalent to employment (added by Pub. L. 98-21 section 322(a)(1), effective in taxable years beginning on or after April 20, 1983). So a case or residual that reads covered does not reach service outside the United States that none of (A)(ii), (B) and (C) reaches: a noncitizen's before 1984, and a nonresident noncitizen's from 1984, that is not on or in connection with an American vessel or aircraft as (A)(ii) states and that no section 433 agreement designates; and a citizen's or resident's service abroad for an employer that is neither an American employer nor a foreign affiliate under a 3121(l) agreement in effect, unless a section 433 agreement designates it. That holds for a Federal employer as for any other: POMS RS 01901.340 A names "services performed outside the U.S. by an alien" as excluded by some other provision of law (review r6 M-5, r7 H-2 and low 9).
